item.title: Effective Field Theory, Starting From the Propagator You Just Learned
item.description: An effective field theory is what you get when you cannot afford the energy to make a heavy particle. This is EFT for someone a few weeks into a first QFT course: one line of algebra on the propagator you already know, one heavy scalar integrated out by hand, then Fermi's theory of beta decay, why non-renormalisable is not an insult, then how a theory predicts the energy at which it will stop working.

item.title: Renormalisation Group VIII: Effective Field Theory
item.description: Part 8 of the renormalisation group course. Why physics works at all without a final theory: effective field theories as a multipole expansion, Fermi's theory as the low-energy shadow of the W boson, what renormalisable really means, why high-energy physics is hard, triviality, asymptotic freedom and safety, naturalness and where to go next.
